subject: Redwood compatibility: OpenAI API parity & next evaluation steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finco.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-07T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood compatibility: OpenAI API parity & next evaluation steps

Hi Sam —

Great talking earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap from my side and suggested next steps so we all have alignment: 

Call recap:
- FinCo goal: validate a migration path from current hyperscaler endpoints to Redwood with minimal changes to prompts/SDKs and predictable token costs.
- Areas of focus: OpenAI-compatible API parity (chat/completions/embeddings), SDK swap effort, prompt diffs (behavioral/regression checks), and throughput/cost comparison vs your current hyperscaler.

Immediate asks we discussed: 
1) Run a smoke compatibility test against our OpenAI-compatible endpoints using your existing prompt set.
2) Run a throughput/cost run (token-level) that mirrors one of your higher-volume batch jobs so we can compare unit economics.
3) Do a small prompt-diff evaluation to flag any canonical differences (stop sequences, tokenization, function calling behavior).

Proposed owners & timeline: 
- Redwood: David will run the hyperscaler vs Redwood throughput/cost comparison using a shared harness. Monica will own the prompt-diff checks and help with a few example SDK migrations.
- FinCo: your engineering team to run the smoke test (we can provide a one-click harness and a short checklist).
- Timeline: aim to have initial results by EOW 2026-07-15. If that works, we can schedule a 30-min readout the following week.

I've attached a short compatibility checklist and an eval instructions doc that walk through the steps and the data we typically ask for. Also sharing a Drive link with the test harness and a small example repo for SDK mapping.

Next steps for you: can you confirm the target batch job you want us to replicate for throughput/cost and loop in your procurement contact for any environment/access needs?

Thanks — looking forward to the tests.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-openai-compat-checklist.pdf, eval-instructions.md

---
On Tue, Jul 7, 2026 at 14:20 Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finco.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call — talk soon.
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Anna Procurement <anna.procurement@annaprocurement@finco.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood compatibility: OpenAI API parity & next evaluation steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That all matches our internal notes. A few clarifying questions before we kick off the runs: 

1) SDK migration: how much of the work is typically a drop-in change vs a small mapping layer? We have a Node/Go microservice that calls the hyperscaler API directly; want to understand time estimate.
2) Function calling & structured outputs: do your OpenAI-compatible endpoints support function calling semantics and reliable JSON-structured outputs (we have a couple prompts that rely on deterministic JSON shapes)?
3) For the throughput test: can you replicate the same model version/sequence lengths we use (we can share a sanitized sample)? We want apples-to-apples unit-cost numbers vs Azure.

I've attached the initial prompt set we'll use for the smoke test (finco-eval-prompt-set.jsonl) and I've looped in Anna from procurement to help with any account provisioning.

If you can confirm owners and a target date (the July 15 goal works), we'll get the dev time scheduled.

—Sam
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finco.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood compatibility: OpenAI API parity & next evaluation steps

Sam —

Great questions; answers below and concrete next steps.

SDK migration effort:
- In most cases it's a small mapping layer (2-5 files) when you already call OpenAI-style endpoints. We provide example client snippets for Node/Go and an SDK shim that mirrors the openai.ChatCompletion/Completions/Embeddings calls. We can send a PR-sized example so your team can estimate work.

Function calling & structured outputs:
- Yes — our OpenAI-compatible chat API supports function calling semantics and we have guidance for robust JSON extraction (post-processing and guardrails). We recommend adding a short validation pass in early runs to catch subtle tokenization differences.

Throughput/cost replication:
- If you can share the sanitized sample (sequence length distribution and batch sizes) David will run the replicated job on our Dedicated infra and produce per-token unit costs vs the hyperscaler. We'll match the model variant where possible and note any model-version-driven deltas.

Owners & timeline (confirmed):
- FinCo: run the smoke compatibility test against the endpoints we provide (we gave a one-click harness link in Drive).
- Redwood: David (david.kim@redwood.com) — throughput/cost test; Monica (monica.patel@redwood.com) — prompt-diff/regression report and SDK examples.
- Target: initial artifacts and readout by 2026-07-15.

I dropped the checklist, prompt set, and eval instructions into the Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinCo-Redwood-Eval. Also linking the HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345678.

Attachment summary: redwood-openai-compat-checklist.pdf (what we need from you), finco-eval-prompt-set.jsonl (your prompt set), eval-instructions.md (how we run the harness).

If you're good with that, we'll schedule a 30-min readout on 2026-07-16 to go over results and decide next steps.

Best,
Marissa
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood compatibility: OpenAI API parity & next evaluation steps

Marissa / Monica —

I'm starting to build the throughput/cost harness today. Quick internal note on plan and asks: 

Plan:
- Ingest FinCo prompt sample (sanitized) and reproduce sequence-length distribution.
- Run three profiles: smoke (low load), steady-state (your normal batch), peak (higher concurrency) and capture latency, p95, token/sec, and per-token billing math.
- Compare to FinCo-provided Azure numbers and produce a short delta sheet.

Asks:
- Need sanitized sample + target batch definition (Sam said they'd share).
- Can we get a short window of access to a FinCo test key or a telemetry export? If procurement prefers, we can accept a sanitized usage CSV instead.
- I'll provision a Dedicated pool and pin a model variant; Monica and I will coordinate the prompt-diff harness runs; I'll drop a spreadsheet with results by 2026-07-15.

I'll also include a short note on migration effort (lines of code impacted, sessions for SDK swap) once I run the initial mapping.

David
